_meta.indication: Treatment of acute, uncomplicated malaria infections due to Plasmodium falciparum in patients of 5 kg bodyweight and above; shown effective in regions where chloroquine resistance has been reported

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, two-center study comparing the 4-dose regimen (over 48 hours) of Coartem to a 6-dose regimen (over 60 hours)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and children (aged ≥ 2 years) in Thailand with acute, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
pivotal_trials.endpoint: 28-day cure rate (clearance of asexual parasites within 7 days without recrudescence by day 28)
pivotal_trials.n: 118 subjects in the 6-dose arm (mITT); 120 in the 4-dose arm
pivotal_trials.result: 28-day cure rate (mITT) was 81% (96/118) for the 6-dose arm vs 71% (85/120) for the 4-dose arm; evaluable cure rate 96.9% (93/96) for the 6-dose arm

pivotal_trials.phase: Randomized, double-blind, comparative, single-center factorial studies
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, comparative single-center studies of Coartem (artemether/lumefantrine) vs each component alone
pivotal_trials.population: Adults in China (Study 1 ages 13-57, Study 2 ages 12-65) with acute, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
pivotal_trials.n: Study 1: Coartem 51; artemether 52; lumefantrine 52. Study 2: Coartem 52; lumefantrine 51
pivotal_trials.result: Study 1 28-day cure rate: Coartem 98.0% (50/51) vs artemether 46.2% (24/52) vs lumefantrine 90.4% (47/52). Study 2: Coartem 96.2% (50/52) vs lumefantrine 88.2% (45/51). 95% CI (Coartem – artemether) on 28-day cure rate: 37.8%, 66.0%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions in adults (>30%): headache, anorexia, dizziness, asthenia, arthralgia and myalgia; in children (>12%): pyrexia, cough, vomiting, anorexia and headache. In adults headache 56%, anorexia 40%, dizziness 39%, asthenia 38%. Key safety concern is QT interval prolongation.
target_moa: Fixed 1:6 combination of two blood schizontocidal antimalarials; artemether (metabolized to active DHA) acts via its endoperoxide moiety, while lumefantrine inhibits formation of β-hematin by forming a complex with hemin; both inhibit nucleic acid and protein synthesis
modality: small molecule (fixed-dose combination of two small-molecule antimalarials)

advisory_committee.vote: Presented to the Anti-Infective Advisory Committee on December 3, 2008; voted 17:1 that Coartem was safe and 18:0 that the product was effective in treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria

orphan_indication.text: Granted orphan designation for the treatment of infections due to Plasmodium falciparum or mixed infections including Plasmodium falciparum on August 31, 2007

citations.quote: This product was granted orphan designation for the treatment of infections due to Plasmodium falciparum or mixed infections including Plasmodium falciparum on August 31, 2007.

summary.text: Coartem was approved under a standard 505(b) NDA with orphan drug designation (granted August 31, 2007), reviewed by the Anti-Infective Advisory Committee (December 3, 2008), and qualified Novartis for a tropical disease priority review voucher under section 524 of the FDCA. Approval carried 14 PMRs and 1 PMC.
